offering_evidence.statement: As part of this change in business focus, and pursuant to the Umbrella Agreement, we have disposed of or agreed to sell all of our legacy container carrier vessels, except for the M/V Itajai Express, and committed to abstain from acquiring additional container vessels.

On January 27, 2025, we entered into the Sales Agreement, under which we may sell, from time to time through Jefferies, as our sales agent, new common shares having an aggregate offering amount of up to $75.0 million as part of our ATM Program.

Specifically, pursuant to the management and administrative services agreements we have entered into with them, our Managers grant us access to human resources, financial and other administrative services, including bookkeeping, audit and accounting services, administrative and clerical services, banking and financial services, client, investor relations, information technology and technical management services, including commercial management of the vessels, vessel maintenance and crewing (not required for vessels subject to bareboat charters), procurement, insurance and shipyard supervision.

We intend to use the net proceeds from the sales of new common shares, after deducting the sales agent’s commissions and our offering expenses, for general corporate purposes, which may include, among other things, the acquisition of new vessels, the repayment or refinancing of all or a portion of our outstanding indebtedness and funding of working capital requirements or capital expenditures.
We provide marine transportation services under medium- to long-term time charters with a range of counterparties.

While we have taken significant steps to change our business focus to concentrate on the LNG/C market, the LPG carriage market and the wider energy transition gas market such as the carriage of low carbon ammonia and LCO2, we can provide no assurances that in the future we will not return to the container market or the dry bulk market, or that we will not explore additional shipping markets beyond the LNG/C and the LPG carriage markets.

we indemnify our Managers for expenses and liabilities they incur on our behalf in the provision of the contracted for services, including, for example, crew, repairs and maintenance, insurance, stores, spares, lubricants and other operating costs;

Although we believe that at the present time no single company has a dominant position in the markets in which we operate, that could change and we may face substantial competition for medium-to long-term charters from a number of experienced companies who may have greater resources or experience than we do when we try to charter our vessels.
Looking ahead, we anticipate active involvement in the development of long-term measures beyond 2030, aligning with the 2028 review of the 2023 IMO GHG Reduction Strategy.

Nevertheless, as most existing vessels are not designed to operate on ultra-low sulphur distillate fuel continuously, we are introducing mitigating measures and or modifications enabling vessels to operate continuously within SECAs.

On December 15, 2023 we agreed to sell the M/V Long Beach Express (68,618 DWT / 5,100 TEU, container vessel, built in 2008 by Hanjin Heavy Industries & Construction Co., Ltd., South Korea) to an unaffiliated party.

On February 14, 2024, we agreed to sell the two remaining Panamax container vessels in our fleet, the M/V Fos Express and the M/V Seattle Express (68,579 and 68,411 DWT, respectively, 5,100 TEU, container vessels, built in 2008 by Hanjin Heavy Industries & Construction Co., Ltd., South Korea) to an unaffiliated party.
